clue.text: Anchor and take in sail, unloading last of fish meal

parts.note: a kedge is a small anchor used for warping a ship

indicators.note: unloading the last means the final letter of the word for taking in sail is dropped

parts.note: to reef is to reduce sail area by rolling part of it in

explanation.surface: A sailor drops anchor and furls sail, having unloaded a catch of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unloading last' drops the F from REEF, leaving REE. KEDGEREE is a dish of flaked fish, rice and eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Kedgeree is a dish of smoked haddock, rice and egg, so it is a meal made with fish.

clue.text: Glove material? Buy it for a child

parts.note: kid is soft leather from young goats, used for gloves
to buy it is slang for to die

explanation.surface: A shopper is told to purchase a pair of leather gloves for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buy it' looks like shopping, but it is British slang for being killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kiddie is an informal word for a young child, a little one.

clue.text: Perform notes framed by French composer in a melancholy manner

parts.note: to do is to perform

indicators.note: framed by means the notes sit inside the composer's name like a picture in a frame

parts.note: Jean-Baptiste Lully, composer at the court of Louis XIV
E and F are musical notes

explanation.surface: Playing music by a French composer, gloomily.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolefully means sorrowfully or mournfully, with a sad air.

clue.text: Poison English archdeacon holding new honour

indicators.note: holding means the first pair of pieces wraps round the abbreviation for new

parts.note: Ven, Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
OM, the Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A churchman is accused of poisoning a rival to get an award.
explanation.definitionFit: To envenom is to put venom into something, to make it toxic.

clue.text: Almost start off before time

indicators.note: start off means the opening letter of the word for almost is removed

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: Nearly setting off ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means ahead of the expected or scheduled moment, premature.

clue.text: It may be added to the drink display

definitions.text: It may be added to the drink
definitions.meaning: a small dash of soda or water poured into whisky
a showy, eye-catching feature, as in a front-page headline

explanation.definitionFit: A dash of mixer is poured into a drink, and a big showy feature in a paper is likewise called this.

clue.text: Supply of tobacco that depended on Napoleon?

definitions.meaning: a twisted roll of tobacco, sold in a long rope
Napoleon is the pig in Orwell's Animal Farm, so what hung from him would be his curly tail; the plait worn by Napoleonic-era soldiers also fits

explanation.definitionFit: Twist tobacco is sold in this plaited form, and a pig such as Orwell's Napoleon has one hanging behind.

clue.text: Member carrying round a bouquet

indicators.note: carrying means the limb holds the round letter inside it

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A club member carries a bunch of flowers around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouquet' suggests flowers, but here it is the scent of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its distinctive smell, its scent or fragrance.

clue.text: Lodging-place helots treated extremely roughly

indicators.note: treated means the letters of helots are processed and rebuilt in a new order
extremely means only the extreme letters, first and last, of the word roughly are taken

explanation.surface: Serfs are badly handled at an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges HELOTS into HOSTEL, and 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'roughly', R and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn or pub where travellers can stay the night.

clue.text: Ship bearing greeting over wide and dangerous waters

indicators.note: bearing means the ship carries the other pieces inside it

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: over means the greeting sits above the abbreviation in this down entry

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A ship signals a hello as it crosses a wide and perilous sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallows are stretches of shoal water, a hazard where ships can run aground.

clue.text: Barkis, presumably, was willin' to do thus as promised

definitions.text: Barkis, presumably, was willin' to do thus as promised

parts.words: Barkis, presumably, was willin' to do thus as promised
parts.note: Barkis, the carrier in Dickens's David Copperfield, famously says 'Barkis is willin''; as a carrier he would bring parcels, and the idiom also means keeping a promise

explanation.surface: Dickens's carrier was willing to keep his word.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: a carrier literally hands over parcels, and figuratively it means doing what was promised.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to fulfil expectations, and a carrier like Barkis literally hands over merchandise.

clue.text: Early childhood's current delusion

parts.note: in means fashionable, current
a fancy is an idle or unfounded notion

explanation.surface: A young child's passing fixation is presented as a grand illusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Infancy is the first stage of life, the babyhood years before boyhood or girlhood proper.

clue.text: Escaping, charge, possibly, for unauthorised disclosure

definitions.meaning: electric charge or liquid seeping out through a fault, 'possibly' marking it as one example
secret information passed on without permission, as to the press

explanation.surface: A fugitive's charge sheet is somehow leaked to the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of current or fluid through a fault is this, and so figuratively is a secret slipping out to reporters.

clue.text: Soldier escorting sweetheart in dance

indicators.note: escorting means the soldier goes along beside the sweetheart, following on here

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart
NCO, non-commissioned officer, a soldier such as a sergeant

explanation.surface: A soldier takes his girlfriend out on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is a passionate Spanish style of dancing with guitar and stamping heels.

clue.text: Scandinavian nominates little fellow for a rise

indicators.note: for a rise means in this down entry the pieces are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to name is to nominate
Ron is a short name for a man, Ronald cut down

explanation.surface: A Nordic boss puts forward a junior colleague for a pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a rise' turns NAMES and RON as one run to give NOR then SEMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norseman is a Viking, an inhabitant of ancient Norway or Scandinavia.

clue.text: Bovine of inferior quality

definitions.meaning: a cow, an animal that moos

explanation.definitionFit: A cow that moos is one that lows, and a lesser grade is placed further down.

clue.text: Discuss changing leader for this informal stroll

indicators.note: changing leader means the first letter of the phrase for discuss is swapped for another

parts.note: to talk about is to discuss

explanation.surface: Debating a casual walk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing leader' swaps the T at the front for W.
explanation.definitionFit: A walkabout is a royal's or politician's informal walk among a crowd.

clue.text: Whimsical fancy revealed in note

definitions.meaning: a peculiar notion or eccentric whim

explanation.surface: An odd idea comes out in a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is an odd whim, and it is also the musical quarter note.

clue.text: The verse Frost recited

indicators.note: recited means the word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: rime is hoar frost

explanation.surface: A line of verse by the poet Robert Frost is read out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frost' looks like the poet but is the icy coating, RIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyme is a name for poetry or verse in general, as in 'rhyme and reason'.

clue.text: One may still be an outsider, however

definitions.text: One may still be an outsider, however

parts.words: One may still be an outsider, however
parts.note: a runner who has gone in for a race may still be a long-odds horse, and one coming in from outside is also still not an insider

explanation.definitionFit: A competitor in a race is one, and may still be a horse with little chance.

clue.text: Roguish as Conservative in mass meeting

indicators.note: in means the other pieces sit inside the word for a mass meeting

parts.note: a rally is a large public gathering

explanation.surface: A Tory at a big political gathering is said to behave roguishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rascally describes the mischievous, dishonest behaviour of a scoundrel.

clue.text: Person who judges the cooking of rarebit

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of rarebit are mixed up as ingredients

explanation.surface: A judge tastes how well a Welsh rarebit has been made.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is a referee or adjudicator who settles disputes.

clue.text: Try excessively when speaking to this matter

indicators.note: when speaking means the phrase is said out loud and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: to try a case in court is to hear it, and too means excessively

explanation.surface: Someone who overdoes it while talking about the issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereto is formal legal language meaning to this document or subject.

clue.text: Criterion, perhaps, for scene of operations

definitions.meaning: the Criterion is a West End playhouse in London's Piccadilly Circus
a surgical operating room, or the area where a war is fought

explanation.surface: A standard is set for where a campaign is conducted.
explanation.definitionFit: The Criterion is a London playhouse, and a hospital's operating room or a war zone carries the same name.

clue.text: Purposeless and discontented?

definitions.meaning: without meaning or aim, as in a hollow gesture
read as dis-contented, having had its contents taken out

explanation.definitionFit: A vacant gesture is meaningless, and a container with its contents removed is vacant too.

clue.text: Adopt half of them and provide support

indicators.note: half of means only part of the word them is used, here its second pair of letters

parts.note: to brace is to prop up or strengthen

explanation.surface: Taking on half of a group and backing them up.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace an idea or cause is to take it up willingly as one's own.

clue.text: Rotten nuisance, bearing such boredom

indicators.note: bearing means the words rotten nuisance carry the letters within them

explanation.surface: A dreadful pest brings on tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is listless weariness, a French word for tedium.

clue.text: Cling to remote possibility, putting novelist's family in conflict

definitions.meaning: to keep wishing for something despite the odds
read literally, members of the family of Anthony Hope, author of The Prisoner of Zenda, set against one another

explanation.surface: A feuding literary family keeps clinging to a slim chance of peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist is Anthony Hope; one Hope set against another is the phrase read literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to keep wishing for an outcome when there is almost no chance of it.

clue.text: Seek ways to make appointments

parts.note: to try is to seek or attempt
STS is the abbreviation for streets, which are ways

explanation.surface: Someone tries to find ways of arranging meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Trysts are secret meetings arranged between lovers, a kind of date or rendezvous.

clue.text: Bitter lot almost destroyed book

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order
almost means the word lot loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A resentful crowd nearly wrecked a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LOT to LO; 'destroyed' then rearranges BITTER and LO.
explanation.definitionFit: A libretto is the written text of an opera, often called its book.
